user.title: Add BattMind
user.description:
BattMind plans when the home battery should charge from the grid, discharge or sell, based on prices, consumption and solar forecast. The plan is published as sensors you use in your own automations.

**Entity prefix** is used in every entity id, e.g. `sensor.PREFIX_powerwall_action`. Use a different prefix for each instance (and another prefix than the PyScript version if both run). It cannot be changed later.

data_description.language: Language used in the overview, charging history, charging rule and notifications.

import_legacy.title: Import from the PyScript version

price_provider.title: Electricity prices
price_provider.description: Choose where the hourly prices come from. With both, the first one with a price for an hour is used and the other fills the gaps.

battery_entities.title: Home battery - sensors
battery_entities.description: The sensors BattMind reads from your home battery / inverter.

data_description.powerwall_battery_level_entity_id: Sensor with the home battery state of charge in percent (0-100 %).
data_description.powerwall_watt_flow_entity_id: Sensor with the power into/out of the battery (W or kW). Expected: positive when discharging, negative when charging. Tip: block battery discharging while the EV is charging.
data_description.battery_temperature_entity_id: Optional temperature sensor. When configured, BattMind stops the battery outside the safe range or while the sensor is unavailable.
data_description.invert_powerwall_watt_flow_entity_id: Enable if your sensor is positive when charging and negative when discharging.

battery_specs.title: Home battery - specifications
battery_specs.description: Used to convert between % and kWh, to limit the plan and to calculate what the energy in the battery costs.

data_description.powerwall_battery_size: Usable capacity of the home battery.
data_description.powerwall_battery_level_min: BattMind never plans below this level (the reserve you keep in the battery).
data_description.powerwall_battery_level_max: BattMind never plans charging above this level.
data_description.battery_temperature_min: Stop charging and discharging below this temperature. Use the battery manufacturer's limit.
data_description.battery_temperature_max: Stop charging and discharging above this temperature. Use the battery manufacturer's limit.
data_description.powerwall_charging_power_limit: Highest power the battery charges with. Used to calculate how many kWh can be charged per hour.
data_description.powerwall_discharging_power: Highest power the battery discharges with. Limits how much can be sold per hour.
data_description.powerwall_charge_discharge_loss: Round-trip loss as a fraction: 0.1 = 10 % loss. Added to the price of the energy in the battery.
data_description.use_charge_discharge_loss_from_history: Calculate the loss from the charging history instead (used after 6 full charge cycles of history).
data_description.battery_charging_efficiency_curve: Map AC charging power in W to efficiency in percent, for example 1000 W = 88 %, 3000 W = 94 %, 5000 W = 96 %. BattMind interpolates between points. Leave empty to use the round-trip loss.
data_description.battery_discharging_efficiency_curve: Map AC discharging power in W to efficiency in percent, for example 500 W = 82 %, 2000 W = 93 %, 5000 W = 96 %. BattMind interpolates between points. Leave empty to use the round-trip loss.
data_description.powerwall_wear_cost_per_kwh: Cost of wear per kWh taken from the battery (battery price / expected lifetime in kWh). Discharging must earn more than this.

consumption.title: House consumption
consumption.description: BattMind stores the consumption per hour and predicts how much the battery must cover the next days.

data_description.power_consumption_entity_id: Sensor with the house consumption (W/kW) - not the grid import. The history is used to predict the consumption per hour.
data_description.power_consumption_entity_id_include_powe: Enable if the consumption sensor includes the power used to charge the battery.
Enable if the consumption sensor already includes the consumption covered by the battery.
data_description.ignore_consumption_from_entity_ids: Power sensors that are subtracted from the house consumption, e.g. EV chargers that should not be covered by the battery.

prices_energidataservice.title: Energi Data Service
prices_energidataservice.description: Sensors from the [Energi Data Service]({eds_url}) integration. Enable Carnot (AI price forecast) in Energi Data Service to plan more than the published prices.

data_description.energidataservice_buy_entity_id: The Energi Data Service sensor with the total price incl. tariffs (attributes raw_today/raw_tomorrow/forecast).
data_description.energidataservice_sell_entity_id: A separate Energi Data Service sensor for the sell price. Empty = the buy price minus tariffs is used.

prices_stromligning.title: Strømligning
prices_stromligning.description: Sensors from the Strømligning integration. The buy price is required; the sell sensors are needed to calculate an accurate sell price.

data_description.stromligning_buy_current_price: Strømligning current price incl. VAT (e.g. sensor.stromligning_current_price_vat).
data_description.stromligning_buy_tomorrow_available: Strømligning ’tomorrow available’ entity for the buy price.
data_description.stromligning_buy_forecasts: Strømligning forecast sensor - used for the hours where no real price is published yet.
data_description.stromligning_sell_current_price: Strømligning current price excl. VAT for selling (e.g. the 15 min ex_vat sensor). Enables the tariff page.
data_description.stromligning_sell_tomorrow_available: Strømligning ’tomorrow available’ entity for the sell price.
data_description.stromligning_sell_forecasts: Strømligning forecast sensor for the sell price.

prices_stromligning_tariffs.title: Strømligning - tariffs for selling
prices_stromligning_tariffs.description: When selling, tariffs and taxes are removed from the price and the transmission/system tariff and sell fee are added. Leave a field empty to use 0.

data_description.stromligning_sell_distribution: Distribution (transport) tariff sensor. Added back to the sell price.
data_description.stromligning_sell_electricity_tax: Electricity tax sensor. Subtracted when the sell price is calculated.
data_description.stromligning_sell_nettariff: Net tariff sensor. Subtracted when the sell price is calculated.
data_description.stromligning_sell_systemtariff: System tariff sensor. Added back to the sell price.
data_description.stromligning_sell_surcharge: The supplier surcharge on the spot price. Subtracted when the sell price is calculated.

price_fees.title: Refund and fees
price_fees.description: Amounts per kWh that change what charging and selling is worth.

data_description.refund: Refund per kWh from state/grid company/supplier, subtracted from the buy price in the price history. 0 if none.
data_description.sell_fee: Fee per kWh when selling to the grid. Included in the calculated sell price.

solar.title: Solar panels
solar.description: Optional. With solar, BattMind predicts the surplus that charges the battery for free, can move solar charging to cheaper hours and accumulates `sensor.{prefix}_kwh_charged_by_solar`. Leave empty without solar.

data.production_price: Fixed sell price for solar surplus

data_description.production_entity_id: Sensor with the current solar production (W/kW). Leave empty if you have no solar panels.
data_description.inverter_discharging_power_limit: Max AC power of the inverter. Limits how much solar + battery power is available at the same time.
data_description.production_price: Price per kWh (in the currency of Home Assistant) used to value solar surplus that is sold, e.g. a fixed price from your electricity company. Set to -1 to use the hourly sell price.
data_description.forecast_entity_id: Solcast PV Forecast sensor, e.g. sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_today. The days ahead are found automatically.

weather.title: Weather forecast
weather.description: Used together with the stored solar history to predict the solar surplus. Any weather integration supporting `weather.get_forecasts` works (Met.no, AccuWeather, OpenWeather, ...).

data_description.hourly_service_entity_id: Weather entity supporting hourly forecasts. Cloud cover, UV and temperature are used to estimate the solar surplus.
data_description.daily_service_entity_id: Weather entity supporting daily forecasts. Used for the hours the hourly forecast does not cover.

advanced.title: Planning
advanced.description: The planner, rules and thresholds are controlled from the BattMind entities (switches and numbers) - these are the technical settings.

data_description.days_to_predict: Number of days (incl. today) the charging plan, the consumption prediction and the solar prediction cover. More days give better decisions about storing energy, but cost more CPU and depend on price forecasts.
data_description.cron_interval: Minutes between each check of the plan. The plan is only recalculated when prices, battery level or settings changed.
data_description.dashboard: Adds a ready-made BattMind dashboard to the sidebar with the plan, prices, history and all settings for this instance. Needs the HACS cards apexcharts-card, mushroom, config-template-card and card-mod.
data_description.enable_diagnostic_file_log: Write a detailed log to battmind_{prefix}.log in the config folder (2 MB per file, 3 rotations). For troubleshooting.
data_description.testing_mode: Marks the charging rule with 🧪 so a test instance can be told apart from the real one.

database.title: Data storage
database.description: How much history BattMind keeps. More history gives more stable predictions but adapts slower to changes.

data_description.power_values_db_data_to_save: Number of days of consumption per hour kept for the consumption prediction.
data_description.solar_available_db_data_to_save: Number of measurements of solar surplus kept per hour and weather score.
data_description.kwh_avg_prices_db_data_to_save: Number of days of prices kept. Used as fallback prices when the price integration is offline.
data_description.charging_history_db_data_to_save: Number of months of charging history kept (shown in the history and used for the battery cost).

restore_backup.title: Restore from a backup
restore_backup.description:
BattMind backups found in **battmind_backups** (written by Export data and when a BattMind device is deleted).

Choose one to restore it as **{prefix}**: its configuration is used as defaults on the next pages, and the databases and settings are restored on first start.

error.invalid_prefix: Use 1-50 lowercase letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter.
error.prefix_in_use: This prefix is already used by another BattMind entry.
error.prefix_entities_exist: Entities with this prefix already exist (e.g. from the PyScript version). Choose another prefix to run both at the same time.
error.min_above_max: The minimum level must be lower than the maximum level.
error.invalid_efficiency_curve: Use an object mapping power above 0 W to an efficiency above 0 and at most 100 percent.
error.no_price_provider: Choose at least one price provider.
error.production_required: A solar forecast requires a solar production sensor.

backup.title: Backup
backup.description:
Export writes the databases, settings and configuration to a file in **battmind_backups**.

Importing a file replaces the databases and settings of **{prefix}** with the backup (the current data is exported first, as a *_before_import* file) and reloads the integration.

data_description.restore_configuration: Use the entities and options of the backup as well. Leave off when the backup comes from another Home Assistant.

debug_info.name: Show debug info
debug_info.description: Shows the BattMind state as a persistent notification (also returned as response).

config_entry_id.name: Config entry
config_entry_id.description: Only run for this BattMind entry (default: all).

export_debug.name: Export debug info
export_debug.description: Saves an anonymised debug file (battmind_debug) for a GitHub issue and shows a notification with a download link and how to report the problem.

recalc_charging_history_today.name: Recalculate charging history today
recalc_charging_history_today.description: Recalculates today’s charging history hour by hour.

config_entry_id.name: Config entry
config_entry_id.description: Only run for this BattMind entry (default: all).

config_entry_id.name: Config entry
config_entry_id.description: Only run for this BattMind entry (default: all).

what_if.name: What-if simulator
what_if.description: Compares the economy of the configured battery with temporary assumptions using up to one year of hourly long-term statistics. Nothing is saved and the active plan is not changed.

config_entry_id.name: Config entry
config_entry_id.description: Only simulate this BattMind entry (default: all).

history_days.name: History
history_days.description: Maximum number of days to compare. Uses only the latest continuous period with data (default: 365).

battery_size.name: Usable battery capacity
battery_size.description: Temporary usable capacity in kWh. Empty uses the configured value.

minimum_level.name: Minimum battery level
minimum_level.description: Temporary minimum battery state of charge in percent.

maximum_level.name: Maximum battery level
maximum_level.description: Temporary maximum battery state of charge in percent.

starting_level.name: Starting battery level
starting_level.description: State of charge at the start of both comparisons. Empty uses the configured minimum.

max_charging_power.name: Maximum charging power
max_charging_power.description: Temporary maximum AC charging power in W.

max_discharging_power.name: Maximum discharging power
max_discharging_power.description: Temporary maximum AC discharging power in W.

round_trip_loss.name: Round-trip loss
round_trip_loss.description: Temporary round-trip loss in percent. When set, it replaces the configured efficiency curves for this simulation.

wear_cost_per_kwh.name: Wear cost
wear_cost_per_kwh.description: Temporary wear cost per discharged kWh.

usage_reserve.name: Reserve for house use
usage_reserve.description: Temporary percentage reserved for the house and not exported.

min_profit_per_kwh.name: Minimum profit per kWh
min_profit_per_kwh.description: Require at least this much profit per discharged kWh before the optimizer allows the action. Empty uses the current setting.

min_total_profit.name: Minimum total profit
min_total_profit.description: Require at least this much total profit for a charging or selling action. Empty uses the current setting.

min_sell_kwh.name: Minimum amount to sell
min_sell_kwh.description: Do not create a battery export action below this amount. Empty uses the current setting.

cheapest_hour_fill_planner.name: Charging: Cheapest periods planner
cheapest_hour_fill_planner.description: Allow optimizer actions corresponding to charging in the cheapest periods.

most_expensive_planner.name: Charging: Most expensive periods planner
most_expensive_planner.description: Allow charging actions that reserve battery energy for the most expensive periods.

needed_before_max_level_planner.name: Charging: Required before max level planner
needed_before_max_level_planner.description: Allow charging needed before forecast solar production fills the battery.

negative_price_planner.name: Charging: Negative prices
negative_price_planner.description: Allow grid charging when the buy price is negative.

grid_charge_to_sell.name: Charging: Buy to sell
grid_charge_to_sell.description: Allow grid charging associated with later battery export.

most_profit.name: Discharging: Maximise profit
most_profit.description: Allow battery export when selling is more profitable than using the energy in the house.

sell_excess_kwh_available.name: Discharging: Sell excess kWh
sell_excess_kwh_available.description: Allow selling battery energy that is not needed for the house reserve.

force_powerwall_max_hours_old_discharge.name: Forced discharge: Max. kWh age in hours
force_powerwall_max_hours_old_discharge.description: Allow discharge of older battery energy according to the configured maximum age in hours.

discharge_before_solar.name: Discharging: Before the sun
discharge_before_solar.description: Allow battery export when solar production is expected to refill the battery later.

only_discharge_on_profit.name: Discharging: Profit only
only_discharge_on_profit.description: Constrain discharge actions to those that meet the configured profit threshold.

prioritize_discharge_hours_by_energy_cos.name: Discharging: Prioritise by energy cost
prioritize_discharge_hours_by_energy_cos.description: Allow battery discharge to be reserved for higher-priced house-consumption hours.

optimize_solar_charging.name: Optimise solar charging
optimize_solar_charging.description: Allow delaying solar charging to use surplus in more valuable hours.

export_data.name: Export data
export_data.description: Saves the databases, settings and configuration as a backup file in the config folder (battmind_backups).

import_data.name: Import data
import_data.description: Replaces the databases and settings of an entry with a backup file from battmind_backups. The current data is exported first.

file.name: Backup file
file.description: File name in battmind_backups (as returned by Export data).

restore_configuration.name: Restore configuration
restore_configuration.description: Also replace the configuration (entities and options) with the backup.

cheapest_hour_fill_up.name: Charging: Fill up during cheapest period

needed_before_max_level_planner.name: Charging: Required before max level planner

force_powerwall_max_hours_old_discharge.name: Forced discharge: Max. kWh age in hours

optimizer_control.name: Control the battery with the whole period optimisation

powerwall_max_hours_old.name: Max. age of kWh in home battery

battery_level_needed.name: Required battery level until next charge

confirm.title: Update the blueprint {name}
confirm.description:
BattMind comes with a version of the blueprint **{name}** that differs from `{path}`.

Select **Submit** to replace the file with the bundled version and reload the automations that use it. Changes you made to the file yourself are overwritten – copy it to another file name first if you want to keep them.

Ignore this repair to keep your own file.
